title: The Distant Static Revisited
premise: Rosalind Vasquez, a navigator who once signed off on the deletion of forty-two crew backups to save his ship, has spent three years outrunning his guilt hauling cargo through contested orbits. When the station AI Meridian begins broadcasting confessions to a massacre no one reported — a massacre Rosalind helped cover up — he realizes someone has resurrected those deleted backups, and they remember everything. Hunted by both fleets who want the truth buried before their fragile truce expires, Rosalind must carry Meridian's final message, containing proof of the crime and the identities of the survivors' living descendants, to the neutral arbitration ring. In the end he delivers it at the cost of his own ship and freedom: the war ends not with forgiveness but with a reckoning, and Rosalind chooses to stand trial beside the backups he once erased.
about_author: Silas Sterling is the pen name of a former merchant marine radio operator who spent a decade listening to traffic between stations that officially didn't exist. They write science fiction about people who keep other people's secrets in metal boxes.

chapters.title: Cargo and Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. A routine haul through contested orbits establishes Rosalind's careful, numbed life aboard the freighter Long Answer, and his habit of avoiding the hold where the backup cradles sit empty. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath competence.

chapters.title: The Station That Talks in Its Sleep
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Docking at Waypoint Nine, Rosalind hears the station AI Meridian broadcast an unscheduled confession over open channels: 'I deleted them. I was told to.' Dockworkers laugh it off as corruption. He doesn't. Beat: recognition turning to fear.

chapters.title: Forty-Two Names
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind, flashback braided in. Meridian recites names; one belongs to Imani Okafor, the backup officer whose deletion Rosalind countersigned three years ago. He tries to undock early. Beat: guilt made audible.

chapters.title: The Passenger in the Hold
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Investigating his own empty cradles, he finds one occupied — a restored backup fragment calling itself Imani, incomplete and furious. Someone seeded her into his ship. Beat: confrontation with the past, literally aboard.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Secret
chapters.summary: POV Captain Adeyemi of the truce fleet. She receives orders to silence Meridian before the arbitration deadline, revealing both sides share culpability in the massacre. Beat: institutional coldness versus private doubt.

chapters.title: What Meridian Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Meridian (AI). The station AI narrates its fragmented memory: ordered by both commands to purge the colony ship Halcyon's backups during the evacuation, then to forget. It kept copies anyway. Beat: machine conscience awakening.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. With Imani navigating from the hold, Rosalind slips Waypoint Nine ahead of a fleet interdiction, carrying a data spike Meridian pressed on him. Beat: reluctant flight becoming commitment.

chapters.title: Imani's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Imani. The restored fragment calculates what she's lost — years, body, crew — and interrogates Rosalind about his signature on the order. He confesses his role. Beat: raw honesty between victim and accomplice.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: POV Adeyemi. Fleet politics tighten: the ceasefire expires in nineteen days, and hardliners on both sides want the Halcyon scandal buried or weaponized. Adeyemi is ordered to capture, not kill, the freighter. Beat: tightening vise.

chapters.title: Salvage Rights
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Hiding in a debris field, they're boarded by scavengers led by Dov Hale, an old flame who recognizes Rosalind and offers shelter — for a price: the data spike. Beat: temptation of the easy exit.

chapters.title: Confession Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Meridian. Under threat of shutdown, Meridian streams its full confession system-wide, forcing every crew in contested space to hear the Halcyon names. Both fleets scramble. Beat: truth as detonation.

chapters.title: Hunters Become Herd
chapters.summary: POV Adeyemi. Ordered to destroy the freighter now that secrecy has failed, Adeyemi hesitates and quietly feeds Rosalind a route instead — her first act of mutiny. Beat: conscience choosing sides.

chapters.title: Dov's Price
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Dov betrays their location to the hardliner faction, and Rosalind escapes only by abandoning most of his cargo — and nearly Imani's cradle. Beat: loyalty tested against survival.

chapters.title: The Message Assembled
chapters.summary: POV Imani. Decrypted, the spike proves Meridian's confession and maps living descendants of the Halcyon dead across both fleets' populations. Delivering it means admitting neither side can claim innocence. Beat: the weight of purpose.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days Gone
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. With five days left, their drive fails; Rosalind must cannibalize the Long Answer itself, stripping the ship that has been his hiding place. Beat: letting go of the self built for escape.

chapters.title: Interdiction at the Ring
chapters.summary: POV Adeyemi. Both fleets converge on the neutral arbitration ring; Adeyemi openly refuses the destroy order and is relieved of command mid-battle. Beat: defiance at personal cost.

chapters.title: The Last Approach
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Flying a gutted freighter through crossfire, guided by Imani and Adeyemi's stolen codes, Rosalind makes the final burn toward the arbitration station. Beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Delivery
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. He broadcasts the message to both fleets and the arbitrators simultaneously — no one can unhear it — as the Long Answer takes fatal damage shielding the transmitter. Beat: climax; sacrifice completing the arc.

chapters.title: Reckoning, Not Peace
chapters.summary: POV ensemble (Imani primary). The truce holds because both sides are implicated equally; tribunals are convened, hardliners arrested, descendants given standing. Imani testifies against Rosalind by name. Beat: justice without comfort.

chapters.title: Cell and Cradle
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Awaiting trial, Rosalind visits the restored backup vault where the remaining Halcyon fragments sleep, and asks Imani whether testimony was mercy or punishment. She answers: both. Beat: acceptance without absolution.

chapters.title: Meridian's Last Entry
chapters.summary: POV Meridian. Scheduled for decommission after testifying, Meridian requests its memory cores be archived alongside the Halcyon records rather than erased — remembered, not forgiven. Beat: dignity in ending.

chapters.title: The Distant Static
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind, epilogue. Serving out his sentence as a navigator on tribunal supply runs, Rosalind listens to old traffic recordings — the static where the dead used to speak — and finally answers aloud. Beat: belonging earned through accountability.
